replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: I've always loved math and physics, finding them logical and beautiful. My background isn't strong academically, but I enjoy seeing how numbers make sense. It's been a reliable friend through my hobbies, helping me understand patterns in climbing and even yoga poses. Math gives me a sense of structure, unlike some subjects that just feel forced on me.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Honestly, yes. Despite enjoying it, the pressure of getting it right creates real stress. My high neuroticism makes math feel high-stakes, even when I'm confident. Sometimes I worry about making simple mistakes or overthinking concepts. It's a mix of genuine interest and that nagging fear of failure that keeps me up at night during exams or problem-solving.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: No, I haven't used AI for learning math recently. I prefer old-school methods like textbooks or online tutorials. While I hear AI helps people, my anxiety makes me hesitant to rely on tools I don't fully understand. I'm skeptical about whether it would truly help or if it might confuse me further when I'm already stressed about concepts.

replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: PCA reduces data to fewer dimensions while keeping most information. First, standardize your data so each variable has mean zero and variance one. Then, find the covariance matrix. Calculate eigenvalues and eigenvectors. The eigenvectors become your new axes. Sort them by eigenvalue size. Project data onto these axes. Don't get anxious—it's just pattern finding, not scary math.
replies.According to you, how can LLMs be used t: LLMs could personalize tutoring, offering instant explanations at each student's level. Instead of one-size-fits-all teaching, AI could adapt to individual struggles. I think it helps reduce anxiety by providing safe, judgment-free practice. But teachers still need to guide. The goal is making math accessible, not replacing human connection or critical thinking entirely.
